outcome: referral to pelvic floor physical therapy or urogynecology
cohort: 334 postpartum women who delivered at an associated hospital and had postpartum visits from June 2020 to April 2022, seen in a university clinic.
finding: The study found a low rate of postpartum screening for pelvic floor disorders and sexual dysfunction within the first year of delivery.
mod_finding: Women with a cesarean delivery were more likely to be screened for PFDs/SD compared to those with vaginal deliveries (73% vs. 58%, p=0.004).
